hook
Last night, your phone lost signal.
This morning... your bank account was empty.
Someone had moved your number to their own e-SIM. And with it, every bank code.
Someone had moved your number to their own eSIM. And with it, every bank code.
problem
DNA already warns customers about scam calls and links.
But a warning is not an answer.
Scared people make the worst move. They call back. Read out a code. Pay the fee.
And small businesses? Most have no security team.
solution
This is Mitta newt. Finnish for: what now?
This is Mitä nyt? Finnish for: “What now?”
You describe what happened, in your own words.
One clear next step. The reason why. And a real person, when it matters.
It even uses what only an operator can see, like SIM changes. But only with permission.

results
On the organisers' own evaluator: five hundred and eighty-eight cases, in three languages.
One hundred percent safe next steps. The included baseline? Sixty.
Zero false alarms. Zero unsafe answers.
And a hundred and thirty-six new situations, written blind by independent AI reviewers: every one handled safely.
impact
So why does this matter for DNA?
It turns every warning into action, at the moment customers are most afraid.
Simple cases close in the chat. Urgent ones reach the right team, already summarised. That can mean fewer calls, and fraud stopped earlier.
Free for every customer, to build trust. A paid security help desk for small businesses. Pricing, to be tested in a pilot.
And it runs on signals only an operator has. That is DNA's advantage.
